transcript.content: Hi, welcome in, and thanks for coming today. Before we dive in, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I'm here because my mind just feels... foggy lately. I work as a library assistant, mostly doing clerical stuff, and recently I can't even seem to keep my place in my old cataloguing notes. It's like I just can't focus. And making decisions, even just deciding what simple task to do next, has become really difficult for me.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately I just... I sit at the kitchen table, and it feels like the color has just gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books, which I usually like, they just make me feel heavy now instead of interested.
How long have you been experiencing this low mood and difficulty concentrating—days, weeks, or longer?

It's been longer than a few weeks. I'd say... probably about three months now. The low mood and that fogginess have been there most days since then. It really seemed to start right around the time I began preparing to leave my job at the library.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or months of low mood and low energy—prior to these last three months?

No, I don't think I have. I mean, sure, I've had a bad day or two over the years, but... nothing like this. I haven't ever felt this low and drained for weeks on end before. It really just started up these last few months.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite since this started, such as sleeping much more or less, or a significant change in your eating?

My appetite is... well, it's about the same, I guess. Nothing major there. But my sleep has definitely changed. I'll go to bed feeling pretty tired, but then I always seem to wake up around four in the morning. And I just can't get back to sleep after that. I just lie there in the dark, thinking about what I'm supposed to do with myself now.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless or excessively guilty about things during this time?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel guilty about anything... and I don't think I'm worthless. It's more just that I feel aimless, I guess. Like I said, I just don't know what to do with my days anymore. But no, no guilt or feelings of being worthless.

Do you notice this low mood and loss of interest even during times when you're not thinking about leaving your job—like on a weekend outing or with friends—or does it mainly come up when the job situation is on your mind?

I'd say it's pretty much all the time. It doesn't really matter if I'm thinking about work or not. Even on a Saturday, if I'm just sitting around the house or trying to do something normal, I still feel that same low energy and lack of interest. It doesn't just switch off when I stop thinking about the job situation. It's just... always there.
Have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself during this time?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had any thoughts about dying or... or hurting myself. It's just a constant low feeling, but I don't want to end things.
Have you noticed a persistent lack of energy or feeling unusually tired, even when you haven't been especially active?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I know I said I had low energy earlier, but I don't feel physically tired or exhausted. It's not like my body is worn out or I need to take naps during the day. It's more of a mental thing, I guess... just not having the drive to do anything, rather than actually feeling fatigued.

latest_inference.note: Symptoms remain consistent with a single depressive episode: pervasive low mood and anhedonia lasting ~3 months, concentration/decision-making difficulty, early morning awakening, no guilt/worthlessness, no fatigue, no suicidal ideation.
